hook: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket, a heavy-lift launch vehicle, suffered a mission-ending catastrophe 10 minutes in.

sections.voiceover: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket, a heavy-lift launch vehicle, suffered a mission-ending catastrophe 10 minutes in.
sections.visual_cue: Graphic showing the Vulcan rocket mid-flight with a countdown overlay of 10 minutes.
sections.sfx_cue: Low, dramatic bass drone that cuts to silence.
b_roll: Stock footage of a rocket ascent in the clouds

sections.voiceover: On November 15, 2026, the Vulcan rocket launched from Cape Canaveral's pad 41 carrying 40 Amazon Leo satellites. But why did the Vulcan rocket mission suddenly end?
sections.visual_cue: Map showing Cape Canaveral and a satellite illustration.
b_roll: NASA footage of Cape Canaveral launch infrastructure

sections.voiceover: However, this failure marks the first total loss in United Launch Alliance's 20-year history.

Flight data reveals an inadequate fuel supply reached the BE-4 engines, the rocket's primary power source. The United Launch Alliance mission ended 10 minutes after liftoff from Cape Canaveral's pad 41.
sections.visual_cue: Diagram of the BE-4 engine fuel lines with an animation showing flow restriction.
sections.sfx_cue: Rising tension, then a dull thud.
b_roll: Technical schematic of the BE-4 engine

sections.voiceover: The November 15, 2026 failure destroyed all 40 Amazon Leo satellites during the Vulcan flight.
sections.visual_cue: Cinematic shot of stars and distant orbital debris.
sections.sfx_cue: Fading echo of a space-themed ambient track.
b_roll: CC space imagery of orbital debris
